analysis:
Reviewed the doc change, the submodule pointer bump and the new opt-in live test. No concrete security regression is supported by the visible evidence.

1) docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md: the only substantive change is the new 'Provider-staged destinations' row at head line 119, plus the date bump at line 3. It describes provider-staged complete-checkpoint imports that create destinations from zeroed host bytes and skip eval/stream fences, so staging no longer waits on MLX-Swift's process-wide evalLock. It also says the import plan charges the largest destination as staging scratch. This is availability and memory-accounting behavior. The DBK3 format, KEK, HMAC lookup tags, TTL, epoch binding and identity bindings (T-041, SEC-035) are unchanged. The doc states that Native-bound imports keep device allocation. Not verified: the source behind it (CheckpointHostZeros.swift, CompleteCheckpointTransfer.swift, PagedCheckpointStorage.swift, CompleteCheckpointImportPlan.swift) is not in the supplied evidence. The next pass should check that zeroed host-memory destinations cannot expose residual plaintext (T-028, A-001) and that the scratch charge cannot be bypassed (TB-007 availability, T-029).

2) libs/mlx-swift-lm: the submodule pointer moves from 14661d9 to c17693f. The diff content is not supplied, so the actual code change is unreviewed. It plausibly implements the staging change documented above, which touches TB-007 and the prefix-cache trust surface. Needs deeper review of the submodule diff.

3) ModelCheckpointRestoreContentionLiveTests.swift is test-only. It is gated on DARKBLOOM_RESTORE_CONTENTION_BENCHMARK=1 and writes a JSON report to a new absolute path. It uses distinct tenant scopes for foreign requests and does not weaken production controls. The report contains the model ID and weight hash, no secrets or prompts.

No threat-model update is required from this evidence. The submodule change is the main coverage limit.
